issue.title: Reports generated together are listed in a different order every day
issue.body:
Six of our scheduled reports are generated in the 06:00 run, all within the
same second. In the recent reports list they come out in a different order
every day, so people hunt for theirs; reports generated together should be in
alphabetical order. I'm fairly sure the cause is
`ORDER BY created_at DESC, id` in `src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts`: breaking ties
by id is as good as random. It should break ties by name.
## Discussion

### priya-s (maintainer) · 2026-11-10
Is this the recent reports list on the dashboard, or the paginated list of
saved reports?

### ops-lead-porto · 2026-11-11
The recent reports list on the dashboard, the one with the number of
recipients on each line. The saved reports list is fine.

input.title: Compare generatedAt at whole-second granularity so same-second reports sort by title
input.body:
File: src/reports.ts

newestFirst already breaks ties by title, but it compares generatedAt in milliseconds, so reports generated in the same second but different milliseconds never tie and come out in an arbitrary order. Change the comparison to use whole seconds (e.g. Math.floor(getTime() / 1000)) before falling back to a.title.localeCompare(b.title). The dashboard's recent list (src/report.tsx) should use this ordering. The ORDER BY in src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts feeds the paginated saved-reports list, which the reporter says is fine, so it should not change.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The reporter's suggested file, src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts, is the query for the paginated saved-reports list, which they say is fine. The dashboard's recent list is ordered by newestFirst in src/reports.ts. It already breaks ties by title, but it compares generatedAt in milliseconds, so reports from the same second rarely tie. The last CI run shows the `newestFirst keeps title order for ties` test in `src/reports.test.ts` passing, because its fixtures share the same millisecond. Draft PR pr-21 proposes comparing at whole-second granularity before falling back to title. I did not run the tests, and the code search index is 47 days old. Search found no caller of newestFirst, so someone should check that the dashboard actually uses it.
